key_insight: VGGT-Edit enables fast, view-consistent 3D scene edits by predicting a residual field on a native 3D scene representation in a single feed-forward pass, avoiding per-view 2D re-projection and iterative optimization.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-quality generalizable feed-forward 3D reconstruction models and interactive editing: previous methods edited each view independently or relied on slow optimization, producing inconsistent multi-view results and poor geometry preservation.
method: Represent the scene with a native 3D field and condition a feed-forward network on a human instruction or edit specification.
Predict a residual field (delta) to apply to the base 3D scene representation so edits are coherent across viewpoints and preserve underlying geometry.
Train end-to-end to produce immediate, multi-view-consistent rendered outputs without per-edit optimization or 2D lifting.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable way to add real-time, consistent 3D editing capabilities to reconstruction pipelines — dramatically reducing latency compared with optimization-based approaches while preserving geometric and view consistency.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input scene → base 3D field → edit instruction → residual-field predictor → edited 3D field → multi-view renderings

paper_title: VGGT-Edit: Feed-forward Native 3D Scene Editing with Residual Field Prediction
paper_authors: Kaixin Zhu, Yiwen Tang, Yifan Yang, Renrui Zhang, Bohan Zeng
